c1-22-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What Machines May Do
c1-22-01.scenario: You have read a text about language models. Károly asks what the machines will do.
c1-22-01.prompt: Tell Károly that machines may soon write many texts.
c1-22-01.target: Könnyen meglehet, hogy a gépek hamarosan sok szöveget írnak.
c1-22-01.english: It may well be that machines will soon write many texts.
c1-22-01.canDo: I can say what may be, must be or may have been true (*könnyen meglehet, hogy*, *nem kizárt, hogy*, *kellett, hogy legyen*, *elveszhetett*).

c1-22-02.title: Communicative Challenge: How the Model Works
c1-22-02.scenario: You have read a text about how a model handles words. Károly asks how it works.
c1-22-02.prompt: Tell Károly what the model does with a sentence, without a passive.
cues: Say what it does with the sentence
c1-22-02.target: A modell tokenekre bontja a mondatot.
c1-22-02.english: The model splits the sentence into tokens.
c1-22-02.canDo: I can describe how a machine handles text without a passive (*a modell feldolgozza, az adatokat tárolják, vektorrá alakul*).

c1-22-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Machines and Poetry
c1-22-03.scenario: You have read a text about machines and poems. Károly asks whether a machine can write a real poem.
c1-22-03.prompt: Tell Károly one thing you are sure of and one thing you only think likely.
cues: Say what the machine does well
Say what stays human, with less certainty
c1-22-03.target: A gép vitathatatlanul jól utánozza a verseket, de a költői mélység feltehetőleg emberi marad.
c1-22-03.english: The machine inarguably imitates poems well, but poetic depth presumably stays human.
c1-22-03.canDo: I can show how sure I am with an adverb (*kétségtelenül*, *vitathatatlanul*, *feltehetőleg*, *vélhetően*).

c1-22-04.title: Communicative Challenge: If We Had Not Collected Texts
c1-22-04.scenario: You have read a text about small languages online. Károly asks why Hungarian texts matter.
c1-22-04.prompt: Tell Károly what would happen if nobody collected Hungarian texts.
cues: Say what we would not do
Say what the machines would not do
c1-22-04.target: Ha nem gyűjtenénk magyar szövegeket, a gépek nem értenék a nyelvünket.
c1-22-04.english: If we did not collect Hungarian texts, machines would not understand our language.
c1-22-04.canDo: I can imagine what would happen to a small language (*ha nem építenénk magyar modellt, … szorulna*; *ha időben elkezdtük volna, … lett volna*).

c1-22-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Old Words
c1-22-05.scenario: You have read the text about Karinthy's Faremidó. Károly asks what happens to old words.
c1-22-05.prompt: Tell Károly how old words leave everyday speech.
cues: Say what happens to old words
c1-22-05.target: A régi szavak fokozatosan kopnak ki a mindennapi beszédből.
c1-22-05.english: Old words gradually wear out of everyday speech.
c1-22-05.canDo: I can say how fast and how deep a change goes (*fokozatosan*, *észrevétlenül*, *visszavonhatatlanul*).

c1-22-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Summing Up Language and Machines
c1-22-consolidation.scenario: You have read a report about language and machines. Károly asks you to sum it up.
c1-22-consolidation.prompt: Tell Károly one thing that may happen to Hungarian and how fast.
c1-22-consolidation.target: Nem kizárt, hogy a régi szavak fokozatosan eltűnnek a beszédből.
c1-22-consolidation.english: It is not out of the question that old words gradually disappear from speech.
c1-22-consolidation.canDo: I can use the words for machine language, small languages and language change.
